svg.title: Chi-square distributions by degrees of freedom
svg.desc: Three chi-square density curves on one pair of axes, for 2, 4 and 10 degrees of freedom. Every curve lies entirely to the right of zero, because a chi-square statistic is a sum of squares and can never be negative. The curve for 2 degrees of freedom is at its highest where the axis starts and falls away from there; the other two rise to a peak and then fall, with the peak further right the more degrees of freedom there are. All three trail off slowly to the right, so all three are skewed right rather than symmetric, and the right skew becomes less pronounced as the degrees of freedom increase: the curve for 10 degrees of freedom is much closer to symmetric than the one for 2. Illustrative data.
svg.text: Positive values only, skewed right, and less so as the degrees of freedom rise
Never negative, always skewed right, and less skewed as df grows.
